newsitem.title: USA: Boeing, McDonnell deal worth about $13.3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, McDonnell deal worth about $13.3 bln.

text.p: Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp said on Sunday they signed a definitive agreement whereby McDonnell Douglas would merge with Boeing in a stock-for-stock transaction.
Under terms of the deal, McDonnell Douglas shareholders would receive 0.65 share of Boeing common stock for each share of McDonnell Douglas common stock, the companies said.
Based on a closing price for Boeing stock of 96-3/4 on December 13, the deal is estimated to be worth about $13.3 billion, the companies said.
The combined company would have about 200,000 employees, including staff from the recent merger of the Rockwell aerospace and defense units into Boeing North American, they said.
It would operate in 27 states with estimated revenues in excess of $48 billion in 1997, making it the largest integrated aerospace company in the world, they said.
The deal was subject to approval by shareholders of both companies and certain regulatory agencies and was expected to close as early as mid-1997, the companies said.
